note: OBSERVED at the last quickSweep run: ms per gate (serial where a serial re-run happened) and exit code. Rewritten every run; used only to choose which gates are under the ship-time budget. Not a claim about the tree -- the register is. `at` is PER ENTRY (v4408): the capture that actually observed that gate. `captured` is this run's stamp and applies ONLY to entries whose `at` equals it -- the rest were not run and say so. `crossings` (v4536) counts CONSECUTIVE sweeps on which a gate came in over budget, and it takes two to evict: one crossing is a reading from one hour, and this box moves 12-36% between hours on unchanged code. A gate that comes back under loses its count entirely. *** v4578 -- THE MS COLUMN HOLDS TWO DIFFERENT QUANTITIES AND NOTHING MARKS WHICH. *** quickSweep writes serialMs ?? parallelMs: a gate under the budget and green has never had a serial run, so its number is a LOADED eight-wide reading; a gate over the budget or red gets a serial confirm, so its number is an ALONE reading. MEASURED over 955 dated under-budget gates the column sits at 1.93x gate-timings, which is the load factor, and over 4 at-or-over ones it sits at 0.98x. v4577 wrote ALONE readings into nine under-budget entries on the reasoning that quickSweep prefers the serial -- true only where a serial exists -- and v4578 re-measured those nine at exactly eight concurrent and replaced them. *** v4579 -- `kinds` SAYS WHICH QUANTITY EACH MS IS: `loaded` is a parallel reading at `workers` gates at once, `alone` is a serial re-run, `capped` is the SIGKILL cap and no runtime at all. quickSweep writes it at the moment it writes the number, where it is KNOWN. Every entry predating v4579 has it INFERRED from the branch rule instead -- under the budget and exit 0 means parallelMs, otherwise serialMs -- and `kindsInferred` names every one of those, because an inference is not an observation. The entries this arc hand-wrote are recorded as OBSERVED and are absent from that list. The two real kinds sit about 1.93x apart, so comparing a ms to anything without its kind compares two quantities.
